A stranger could keep you from resetting a forgotten password. That is fixed, and a reset now also removes passkeys, tokens and keys.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Somebody else could stop a password reset.** Five wrong codes used up the code in the container log, so anybody who could open the login page could keep you from resetting by guessing after each of your requests. The code now has twelve characters, and wrong guesses no longer use it up.
- **Behind a reverse proxy, other people's failed logins blocked the reset.** The reset shared the login's limit of five failures a minute, which counts per address, and behind a proxy every visitor has the proxy's address. The right code now always goes through, and only wrong codes are slowed down.
- **The answer told whether a code was still valid.** A wrong code and an expired one got different answers. Both now get the same one.
- **A password change could undo a reset.** A change started before a reset and saved after it overwrote the new password. It is now refused when a reset or another change came in between.

## ⚡ Improved

- **A reset now removes every other way in.** Besides switching two-factor authentication off and ending every other session, it deletes every passkey and revokes every API token, MCP key and OAuth sign-in, so nothing somebody else set up survives it. The login page lists what was removed. **Add your passkeys again** under Settings, Security, and create new tokens and keys where you need them.
- **Whoever can read the container log can reset the password.** The 9.9.2 notes said that takes access to the host. It does not: a log viewer such as Dozzle, a container given the Docker socket (read-only is enough) or a log shipper can read the code as well. Give those only to people you would trust with the password.

## 🌐 Translations

- The new reset messages in all 42 languages, and the reset paragraph of the configuration page in all 26 documentation languages.

## Upgrading

- **Nothing has to be changed.** If you reset your password, add your passkeys again afterwards.
